items.headline: Haaland captain in Gameweek 1 bench boost draft built around Arsenal defence
items.summary:
The near-final Gameweek 1 draft is set up for an immediate bench boost, with the chip used early to avoid carrying a bloated squad later and to take advantage of more reliable opening-week fixtures. The structure is a 3-4-3, captained by Erling Haaland at home to Bournemouth, with Calvert-Lewin and João Pedro completing a template front three. The plan broadly targets Gameweeks 1-3, with a possible wildcard around the first international break if fixture swings demand it.

The biggest shift is a move into triple Arsenal after the Community Shield reinforces confidence in their defence. Ben White and Riccardo Calafiori are paired at the back, with Arsenal attacker Solis added in midfield. White is preferred for reliable minutes while Jurrien Timber is out, while Calafiori offers the best goal threat among the cheaper Arsenal defenders but carries a substitution risk around the 60-minute mark. Solis is backed because of his strong pre-season assist threat and likely role on Arsenal’s left, though team leaks may still force late changes.

Harry Maguire is preferred to Luke Shaw because of his multiple routes to points: clean sheets, set-piece goal threat, bonus and defensive contribution potential. Leif Davis is selected for assist upside, while Joe Rodon and Brentford’s Sangare are valued as dependable bench-boost and rotation picks who can cover awkward fixtures in Gameweek 2. Pascal Gross remains in midfield despite Brighton signing Promise David, with the view that Gross may lose penalties but could gain assist potential from having a strong finisher to target.

Rate My Team projects the bench boost side at 70 points in Gameweek 1 with a 95% rating, although it marginally prefers Bruno Fernandes over Haaland as captain on expected points. Bruno is still viewed as the standout Gameweek 2 captain, while Gameweek 3 may prompt two free transfers towards Manchester City assets for their Coventry fixture, potentially involving an Arsenal defender or a Manchester United player making way. Looking further ahead, Chelsea’s Gameweek 4 home match against Hull puts João Pedro firmly in the captaincy conversation, while Cole Palmer is not considered essential despite algorithmic support.
key_points: Bench boost is planned for Gameweek 1 rather than being saved, with the squad built for Gameweeks 1-3 and a possible wildcard around Gameweek 4.
Haaland is the Gameweek 1 captain at home to Bournemouth, despite Rate My Team narrowly rating Bruno Fernandes higher on expected points.

Pascal Gross stays despite Promise David’s arrival at Brighton, with lost penalties offset by possible extra assist potential from a better striker target.

Joe Rodon and Brentford’s Sangare are kept as reliable rotation pieces who can step in during Gameweek 2 and support the bench boost.

items.headline: No-Haaland Gameweek 1 draft loads up on Bruno Fernandes, Arsenal defence and bench boost depth
items.summary:
A Gameweek 1 squad without Erling Haaland frees up enough money to build a much deeper Fantasy Premier League team, with the main argument resting on value, form and early chip strategy. Haaland’s £15.5m price tag is questioned after his Community Shield display, and the draft leans into a Bench Boost in Gameweek 1 to maximise points across all 15 players rather than concentrating budget in one premium forward.

The goalkeeper pairing remains Bart Verbruggen and Kinski, mainly because they rotate well and both help support the opening-week Bench Boost plan. In defence, the extra Haaland money allows more spending: Gabriel comes in at £8.0m, joined by Riccardo Calafiori, who could alternatively be Ben White, and Harry Maguire. Diop and Muharemovic sit on the bench but are still intended to contribute in Gameweek 1 if the chip is active.

Midfield is where the no-Haaland structure starts to look powerful. Bruno Fernandes is treated as close to essential in this setup, with the point made that managers may not want to go without both him and Haaland, but dropping one of the two enables a much stronger all-round squad. Bryan Mbeumo, Antoine Semenyo, Arsenal’s popular new £6.5m signing Soucek, who has supplied plenty of pre-season assists, and Liverpool’s Dominik Szoboszlai complete a well-funded midfield.

Up front, the draft goes with Joao Pedro, Thiago and Dominic Calvert-Lewin instead of Haaland. The appeal is that all three look sharp and arguably enter the season in better form than the Manchester City striker. The clear risk is Gameweek 3, when Haaland has Coventry at home, so this route requires either a plan to buy him back or the nerve to bet against him through an attractive early fixture.
key_points: Erling Haaland is left out despite his £15.5m premium status, with his Community Shield performance used as part of the case against him.

items.title: FINAL FPL TEAM from THREE Champions! 🏆
items.headline: Haaland split defines Gameweek 1 as champions back early Bench Boosts and aggressive wildcards
items.summary:
Three former FPL winners land on strikingly different Gameweek 1 plans, with Erling Haaland the main fault line. Jonas builds the boldest draft: David Raya, Gabriel and further defensive coverage form a triple Arsenal back line, while he also attacks early fixture clusters with heavy exposure to Liverpool, Coventry and Manchester United. The headline call is no Haaland, with Bruno Fernandes captain in Gameweek 1 and a Bench Boost planned for Gameweek 2 before a likely Wildcard in Gameweek 3, when Haaland’s home fixture against Coventry makes him close to unavoidable in this strategy.

The logic behind Jonas’ approach is covariance and rank swing: if Arsenal clean sheets land, Liverpool attackers fire and Haaland blanks early, the upside is enormous. The trade-off is that the plan almost forces an early reset, and a Gameweek 3 Wildcard creates awkward timing around Chelsea assets, who face Arsenal that week before a better run. There are also minutes risks, especially around Vertonghen, while Richarlison’s appeal depends on Spurs’ attacking signings and Solanke’s fitness. Bruno Fernandes is treated as essential because of his many routes to points, while Thiago is flagged as overlooked and Pascal Gross becomes a strong 5.5m option if he has penalties.

Joshua Bull takes the opposite route structurally: Haaland and Bruno are both in, the starting XI is stacked, and the bench is deliberately light. His draft includes Kinski, Pedro Porro, Maguire, Calafiori and Davies at the back, with Mbeumo, Bruno, Foden, João Pedro and Haaland central to the plan. He is not planning an early Bench Boost, arguing that transfers and the first Wildcard should create a better chip opportunity once teams, roles and minutes are clearer. Bruno’s 12.0m price is a concern, but starting with him protects against a fast start and makes it easier to move down than to scramble up.

Ben Crabtree lands between the two extremes: he keeps Haaland, avoids Bruno, sets up a 3-4-3, and also targets a Gameweek 2 Bench Boost followed by a likely early Wildcard. His attack is built around Haaland, João Pedro and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, with Calvert-Lewin backed as the safest 6.0m forward thanks to pre-season form and fixtures. Cheap defenders such as Mykolenko, Van Hecke, Vardy and Calafiori are accepted because the plan is short term, though Vardy and Calafiori carry rotation risk. In midfield, Mbeumo is considered safer, Cunha’s Gameweek 1 start needs monitoring, Rogers is benchable in Gameweek 1 with a view to Gameweek 2, and Diogo Jota enters as an upside pick.
key_points: Jonas goes without Haaland, captains Bruno Fernandes in Gameweek 1, Bench Boosts in Gameweek 2 and plans to Wildcard in Gameweek 3 to buy Haaland for Coventry at home.
Jonas’ no-Haaland structure enables aggressive triples on Arsenal defence, Liverpool attack, Coventry and Manchester United, but it depends heavily on early clean sheets and fixture swings landing.
Joshua Bull starts with both Haaland and Bruno, prioritises a powerful XI over bench depth, and is not planning an early Bench Boost.
Joshua sees Bruno at 12.0m as expensive but strategically safer to own early because selling down is easier than buying him after a haul.
Foden is Joshua’s main uncertainty, with Szoboszlai or a cheaper 6.0m midfielder possible alternatives to free money for squad depth.

items.headline: Calvert-Lewin locks in as 3-4-3 and Gameweek 1 bench boost reshape the FPL template
items.summary:
The late Gameweek 1 template is moving sharply toward a 3-4-3 built around Erling Haaland, João Pedro and Dominic Calvert-Lewin. Among engaged FPL managers, 3-4-3 rises from 42% to 56% as managers move money out of the fifth midfielder slot and into a stronger forward line. Calvert-Lewin, now in 75% of engaged drafts, is treated as close to essential at £6.0m, while João Pedro is almost universal and Haaland remains highly owned despite growing doubts.

Chip strategy is driving much of the structure. More than 75% of engaged managers plan to bench boost in the first two gameweeks, with 55% now targeting Gameweek 1 and 20% Gameweek 2. That makes £4.5m goalkeepers Kinski and Verbruggen the dominant pairing because they combine budget pricing with strong opening fixtures: Aston Villa at home and Brentford away. The early wildcard also gains momentum, with Gameweek 6 the favoured window because it follows the international break and gives managers five weeks of data, price movement opportunities and injury information.

Defence is where engaged managers are trying to gain the biggest edge over the wider game. Calafiori surges to 75% ownership after strong attacking pre-season signs, although his repeated 59-minute outings create some minutes concern. Harry Maguire is preferred to Luke Shaw by many because he looks nailed, scores well for defensive contribution and carries set-piece threat as Manchester United’s main aerial target. Diop becomes popular for a Gameweek 1 bench boost thanks to a £4.0m price and a home fixture against Sunderland, while Rodon is a budget enabler and Muramovic is viewed as the upgrade if funds allow. Vardyol and Williams are losing favour as managers redirect money into better-value centre-backs.

In midfield, the template leans heavily on double Manchester United with Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo. Szoboszlai’s ownership falls sharply as managers question his attacking positioning, with Florian Wirtz gaining as a Liverpool alternative. Pascal Gross remains a common value pick, while the big late mover is Solly, whose pre-season form pushes him into many drafts despite some concern that Gameweek 1 is flattering the fixture outlook. Captaincy is no longer a runaway Haaland call: he still leads at 53%, but that is down heavily, while Bruno Fernandes rises to 37% as managers weigh Haaland’s subdued pre-season against Bruno’s appeal.
key_points: The preferred structure is now 3-4-3 with Haaland, João Pedro and Dominic Calvert-Lewin as the dominant front three.
Gameweek 1 bench boost is the leading chip plan, with Kinski and Verbruggen the favoured £4.5m goalkeeper pairing for strong opening fixtures.
Gameweek 6 is the popular early wildcard slot because it follows the international break and comes after five gameweeks of information.
Calafiori rises sharply in ownership due to attacking threat, but his pre-season minutes remain a small risk.
Harry Maguire is favoured over Luke Shaw for nailed minutes, defensive contribution potential and set-piece threat.
Diop is a Gameweek 1 bench boost enabler at £4.0m, while Rodon is the cheaper fallback if Muramovic is unaffordable.
Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo form the core midfield double-up, with Wirtz gaining ground as Szoboszlai loses support.

items.title: FPL Gameweek 1 Preview 🔥 Bruno captain 👀 Sell Groß 🤔
items.headline: Haaland edges Fernandes for Gameweek 1 captaincy despite Doku injury and City doubts
items.summary:
Manchester United's early fixtures remain the main attraction, with Hull away in Gameweek 1 and Ipswich at home in Gameweek 2 still worth targeting. Benjamin Šeško and Matthijs de Ligt are back training with the main group, but neither is expected to go straight into the starting XI after time out, so Harry Maguire still looks usable in the short term. Imbula remains a minutes risk, especially with Šeško returning and other attacking reshuffles possible, but the expectation is that he starts the first two matches as United's number nine before managers reassess from Gameweek 3 onward.

Jeremy Doku's reported calf injury makes him an avoid or sell before Gameweek 1 and slightly weakens Manchester City's attacking outlook. Sávio now looks extremely secure for minutes, while Phil Foden becomes a more viable short-term punt if City use Sávio on the left and Foden or Cherki on the right. Even so, the loss of Pep Guardiola, Rodri and other senior players is seen as a downgrade rather than a reason to abandon City assets: Bournemouth at home, Palace away and Coventry at home are still strong enough fixtures to justify Haaland and at least some City exposure.

Captaincy comes down mainly to Haaland at home to Bournemouth or Bruno Fernandes away to Hull. Haaland is the default pick because backing against him at the Etihad requires a very strong reason, but Fernandes is a serious alternative because Hull profile as a weak promoted side and most Haaland-and-Bruno owners are likely to captain Haaland. Arsenal alternatives carry too much minutes risk: Saka may not be fully ready, Havertz can be hooked early for Julian Alvarez, and Saliba is more of a bold punt than a recommended captain.

João Pedro is not essential, but he is still one of the best forward picks at 7.5m and is preferred in most Gameweek 1 structures, especially for managers not committing to an early wildcard. Arsenal away in Gameweek 3 is awkward, but Hull at home in Gameweek 4 makes him a player many will want quickly and possibly captain. Pascal Gross remains a strong 5.5m Brighton option even after the signing of Promise David, though David's better penalty record creates a real risk that Gross loses spot-kicks. Elsewhere, Raya is a premium set-and-forget goalkeeper if budget allows, Dewsbury-Hall is safe but less appealing than a cheaper penalty-taking Iheanacho/Enjai type if he stays, Schade is preferred to Dango for value, and Szoboszlai remains a reliable all-rounder even if Wirtz offers more upside for 0.5m extra.
key_points: Captaincy: Haaland is the current pick at home to Bournemouth, but Bruno Fernandes away to Hull is a legitimate differential and would be comfortable for no-Haaland teams.
Man United: Šeško and De Ligt are back in group training but are not expected to start the Hull and Ipswich fixtures; Maguire and Imbula remain viable short-term picks.
Imbula: likely starts Gameweeks 1-2 as United's number nine, but early substitutions and longer-term competition from Šeško make him an aggressive pick.
Man City: Doku should be removed after a reported calf injury; Sávio looks close to nailed, while Foden gains short-term appeal without becoming secure.
João Pedro: not essential, but high ownership, strong minutes and Hull at home in Gameweek 4 make him difficult to ignore unless wildcarding early.
Brighton: Promise David is one to monitor rather than buy for Gameweek 1, but his penalty record may threaten Pascal Gross's spot-kick appeal.
Arsenal: Raya is worth considering immediately if budget allows; Saka and Havertz carry captaincy/minutes concerns, while Saliba is a fine short-term punt but not essential.
Mid-price calls: Schade is preferred to Dango for the 0.5m saving; Szoboszlai is safer and cheaper than Wirtz, though Wirtz has the higher upside if money is spare.

In attack, Soler and Odegaard both impress and look appealing at £6.5m, but Kai Havertz is an avoid because Nkunku’s fitness creates uncertainty over who starts.","Bruno Fernandes misses two penalties in pre-season, but there is no expectation that he loses spot-kicks. Mbeumo is benched in Manchester United’s final friendly, yet he is still expected to start as the number nine against Hull and Ipswich; Cunha likely plays instead because he needs minutes. Elsewhere, Minteh’s two-to-three-month absence opens a route to minutes for Diego Gomez if fit, though a post-match limp makes him one to monitor rather than lock in.","Brentford end pre-season with a 7-0 win, strengthening the case for their attackers. Dango and Schade look like high-upside differentials, while Thiago remains a solid pick. Ajer starts and is highlighted as a useful £4.5m defender with defensive contribution potential. Chelsea’s final friendly brings Rogers straight back into the XI, where he is expected to stay, and a wing-back system makes Pellistri an interesting option if that shape carries into Gameweek 1.","At Spurs, Spence’s sale and Udogie’s lack of fitness point to major minutes for Robertson at just £4.5m in defence. Solanke misses the final friendly, putting Richarlison in line to start at number nine and possibly take penalties. For Ipswich, O’Shea scores but plays right-back, which may limit his defensive contribution appeal, making Diop the preferred £4.0m defender from their squad.","key_points":["Haaland, Anderson and Odegaard all get pre-season minutes and are expected to start Gameweek 1, though full fitness remains uncertain.","Gabriel and Raya are the safest Arsenal defensive picks; Mosquera, White and Castagne offer £5.5m value.","Soler and Odegaard impress at £6.5m, while Havertz is a fade because Nkunku threatens his starting security.","Bruno Fernandes is still expected to stay on penalties despite two pre-season misses.","Mbeumo should start up front for Manchester United against Hull and Ipswich despite being benched in the final friendly.","Minteh is out for two to three months, boosting Diego Gomez’s minutes prospects if he recovers from a reported limp.","Brentford’s Dango and Schade are differential attackers, Thiago remains solid, and Ajer looks useful at £4.5m.","Richarlison is set to start as Spurs’ number nine with Solanke absent and may be on penalties."]}

items.title: NO HAALAND! 🚫 Lee's New FPL GW1 Team!
items.headline: Haaland-less Gameweek 1 draft hinges on early Bench Boost escape route
items.summary:
The current Fantasy Premier League draft leaves Erling Haaland out, with the money spread across a squad designed to look stronger overall and to support an early Bench Boost. The logic is that removing the Manchester City striker opens up enough budget to build a more balanced 15-man squad rather than concentrating so much value in one premium asset.

The risk is obvious: Haaland can punish non-owners immediately in Gameweek 1. The plan is not dogmatic, though. There is a built-in escape route: if the no-Haaland structure proves wrong, he can be brought back on an early Wildcard around Gameweeks 4, 5 or 6, depending on how quickly the damage becomes clear.

There is also still a chance Haaland returns before the season starts. A recent training clip makes him look sharp, and his playing style reduces some concern over match fitness. Unlike high-energy runners such as Doku or Semenyo, Haaland does not need to spend 90 minutes constantly sprinting; he can drift, conserve energy, then explode into space and finish chances.

So the decision remains finely balanced. The current preference is to attack the opening weeks with a deeper, Bench Boost-ready squad, but Haaland’s sharpness and explosive scoring potential mean he is not being ruled out for Gameweek 1.
key_points: Current draft excludes Erling Haaland to free funds for a stronger overall squad.
The structure is built with an early Bench Boost in mind, prioritising depth across all 15 players.
If going without Haaland backfires, the intended correction is an early Wildcard in Gameweek 4, 5 or 6.
Haaland is still under consideration for Gameweek 1 after looking sharp in training.
Fitness concerns are viewed as less significant because Haaland’s game relies on short explosive movements rather than constant running.
The core trade-off is squad balance and chip strategy versus the immediate captaincy and haul risk of owning Haaland.
